#2922 -- the reporter's literal repro, run on ground truth
==========================================================

The issue says:

    Repro: e.g., open PixTest.cpp, find the "Compile" function and change the
    -Od to -O1, then run the taef tests with /name:PixTest::PixStructAnnotation_*

That instruction can no longer be followed literally, because the edit it asks for has
already been made upstream. PixTest.cpp now runs EVERY PixStructAnnotation_* test at both
-Od and -O1 unconditionally:

    tools/clang/unittests/HLSL/PixTest.cpp
      static const OptimizationChoice OptimizationChoices[] = {
          {L"-Od", false},
          {L"-O1", true},
      };

and the three per-test opt-outs that used to stop the -O1 half from running are gone.
Commit c0676c7ca deleted all three:

    $ git show c0676c7ca -- tools/clang/unittests/HLSL/PixTest.cpp \
        | grep -c "don't run -O1 test until pointer types are dealt with"
    3
    $ grep -c "don't run -O1 test" tools/clang/unittests/HLSL/PixTest.cpp
    0

The line they removed read, verbatim:

    break; // don't run -O1 test until pointer types are dealt with by value-to-declare pass

So "run the taef tests" IS the -O1 test today. Running them:

    $ cd C:\prj\DirectXShaderCompiler\build\Debug\bin
    $ "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Testing\Runtimes\TAEF\x64\TE.exe" \
          ClangHLSLTests.dll /name:PixTest::PixStructAnnotation_*

Ground truth: build\Debug\bin, dxcompiler.dll 1.10(5433-ab540090)(1.9.0.5433), main @ ab5400907.
Full unedited console output: manual-case-taef-raw.txt (1953 lines).

    StartGroup: PixTest::PixStructAnnotation_Lib_DualRaygen

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT EVIDENCE OF
-----------------------------------
It IS evidence that the reported repro, executed as written against today's tree, does not
fail. Three of these tests (_FloatN, _SequentialFloatN, _EmbeddedFloatN) are the ones whose
-O1 half used to be skipped for exactly this bug, and their -O1 halves now run and pass.

It is NOT a release history: ClangHLSLTests.dll is built from main and loads main's
dxcompiler.dll, so this cannot say anything about v1.6.2112 or any other release. The
release history is in manual-case-release-history.txt, which drives each release's own
dxcompiler.dll through dxopt -external.

It is also not a substitute for the direct measurement. A passing test suite could in
principle pass for the wrong reason -- for instance if the -O1 configuration silently stopped
reaching the pass. manual-case-release-history.txt rules that out by showing the pass output
itself: main's -O1 run does contain the pointer-typed llvm.dbg.value on input and does emit
two llvm.dbg.declares on output.
